label: complex symmetric
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{complex symmetric}
	Let $T\in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$ and $C$ be a conjugation on $\mathcal{H}$. Then $T$ is said to be $C$-symmetric if $T^*=CTC$. Equivalently, $T^*C=CT$, or $TC=CT^*$, and $T$ is said to be a $C$-skew-symmetric if $CT^*C=-T$.

label: conjugate normal
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{conjugate normal}
	An operator $T\in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$ is said to be conjugate normal if $C|T|C=|T^*|$ for some conjugation $C$ (in this case, $T$ is said to be $C$-normal).

label: ptak_charac
title: Theorem
body_md:
\cite[Theorem 2.3]{Ptak}\label{ptak_charac}
		Let $C$ be a conjugation on $\mathcal{H}$, and let $T\in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$. Then the following are equivalent:
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item $T$ is C-normal,
			\item $T^*$ is $C$-normal.
			\item $CTC$ is $C$-normal.
			\item $CT^*C$ is $C$-normal.
			\item $CT^*T=TT^*C$.
			\item $CT(CT)^{\#}=(CT)^{\#}CT$.
			\item\label{norm condition C-normal} $\left\|TCx\right\|=\left\|T^*x\right\|$ for $x\in \mathcal{H}$.
			\item $\left\|T^*Cx\right\|=\left\|Tx\right\|$ for $x\in \mathcal{H}$.
			\item $T_{+}:=\frac{1}{2}(CT+T^*C)$ and $T_{-}:=\frac{1}{2}(CT-T^*C)$ commute.
			\item $T_{+}:=\frac{1}{2}(TC+CT^*)$ and $T_{-}:=\frac{1}{2}(TC-CT^*)$ commute.
		\end{enumerate}

title: Theorem
body_md:
Let $S, T\in \mathcal{B}_{a}(\mathcal{H})$, and $C$ be a conjugation on $\mathcal{H}$. Then the fallowing are equivalent:
	\begin{enumerate} 
		
		\item\label{AD1}  $\text{ran}(T) \subseteq \text{ran}(S)$.
		
		\item\label{AD2}  $T T^{\#} \leq S S^{\#}$.
		
		\item\label{AD3} $T=S R$, where $R=CDC$ for some $D \in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$.
	\end{enumerate}
	Moreover, for such an operator $R$, we have $\ker R=\ker T$ and $\overline{\text{ran}}(R)=(\ker S)^\perp. $

\label{compression C-normal}
	Let $T\in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$. If $\mathcal{M}$ is a reducing subspace of $T$ and $T|_\mathcal{M}=0$, then $T\in (\mathcal{GS})$ if and only if $T|_{\mathcal{M}^\perp}\in (\mathcal{GS})$.

title: Corollary
body_md: Let $T\in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$ be normal. Then $T\in (\mathcal{GS})$  if and only if $T|_{(\ker T)^\perp}\in (\mathcal{GS})$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Since $T$ is normal, $\ker T$ is a reducing subspace for $T$ (cf. \cite[Proposition 5.6]{Conway:Book:Functional analysis}). Hence by \cref{compression C-normal}, the conclusion follows.

title: Lemma
body_md: Let $C$ be a conjugation on a separable complex Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$. Suppose that $T\in \mathcal{B} (\mathcal{H})$ is a $C$-normal operator. If $T$ is normal, then $T|_{(\ker T)^\perp}$ is $C_2$-normal, where $C_2:(\ker T)^\perp\rightarrow(\ker T)^\perp$ is a conjugation.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $T$ is normal, we have $\ker T=\ker T^*$. Write $\mathcal{H}=\ker T\oplus(\ker T)^\perp$. Then $T$ can be written as $T= \begin{bmatrix}
	0&0\\
	0&A
	\end{bmatrix}$, where $A:(\ker T)^\perp\rightarrow(\ker T)^\perp$.
	
	Now $T$ is $C$-normal which implies $C\ker T=\ker T^*=\ker T$. Therefore, $C$ can be written as $C=\begin{bmatrix}
	C_1&0\\
	0&C_2
	\end{bmatrix}$, where $C_1:\ker T\rightarrow\ker T$ and $C_2:(\ker T)^\perp\rightarrow(\ker T)^\perp$. Note that $C_2$ is also a conjugation on $(\ker T)^\perp$ and $CT^*TC=TT^*$ implies that $C_2A^*AC_2=AA^*$ which implies $A:=T|_{(\ker T)^\perp}$ is $C_2$-normal.
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md: Let $C$ be a conjugation, and $T\in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$ be $C$-normal. Suppose that $S_2=T^*T+TT^*$, then $S_2\cong N\oplus N^*\oplus A$, where $N$ is normal operator and $A$ is self-adjoint operator.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Since $T$ is $C$-normal, the operator $S_2$ satisfies $CS_2C=S_2$. Hence, by using \cite[Theorem 5]{Wang:Xie:Yan:Zhu}, the conclusion follows.

label: CTC=-T
title: Question
body_md:
\label{CTC=-T}
	\emph{Characterize all normal operators $T$ satisfying $CTC=-T$ for some conjugation $C$.}
head: environment

label: key-lemma
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{key-lemma}
	Let $T\in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$ be normal and $C$ be a conjugation such that $CTC=-T$, or equivalently, $CT+TC=0$. Then $C\text{ran}E_{T}(\Delta)=\text{ran}E_{T}(-\Delta^*)$, where $\Delta=\Sigma_1\cap\sigma(T)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $CTC=-T$, we have $\sigma(T)=-\sigma(T)^*$. Let $f\in C(\sigma(T))$, the space of all continuous functions defined on $\sigma(T)$, define $f^*(z)=\overline{f(-\bar{z})}$ for all $z\in \sigma(T)$. Then the function $f^*\in C(\sigma(T))$. For $g(z)=\alpha z^n\bar{z}^m$, it follows that
	\[ Cg(T)C=C(\alpha T^n(T^*)^m)C=\bar{\alpha}(-T)^n(-T^*)^m=g^*(T).\]
	Since all bivariate polynomials in $z$ and $\bar{z}$ are uniformly dense in $C(\sigma(T))$, it follows that
	\begin{equation}
		Cf(T)C=f^*(T), \quad\text{for all} \,f\in C(\sigma(T)).
	\end{equation} 
	
	Let $\chi_{\Delta}$ be the characteristic function of $\Delta$ belongs to $L^\infty(\mu)$, where $\mu$ is a scalar-valued spectral measure for $T$. Thus there exits a sequence $\{f_n\}$ in $C(\sigma(T))$ such that $f_n\rightarrow\chi_{\Delta}$ and $f^*_n\rightarrow\chi_{-\Delta^*}$ in the weak$^*$-topology of $L^\infty(\mu)$. Thus by functional calculus for normal operators (cf. \cite[Theorem 8.10]{Conway:Book:Functional analysis}), we get $f_n(T)\rightarrow\chi_{\Delta}(T)$ and $f^*_n(T)\rightarrow\chi_{-\Delta^*}(T)$ in the weak operator topology. Therefore, we obtain $C\chi_{\Delta}(T)C=\chi_{-\Delta^*}(T)$, that is, $CE_T(\Delta)C=E_T(-\Delta^*)$, and hence the desired conclusion follows.
head: environment

title: Theorem
body_md: Let $T\in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$ be a normal operator. Then there exists a conjugation $C$ such that $CTC=-T$ if and only if $T\cong T_1\oplus (-T_1^*) \oplus (iT_3)$, where $T_1$ is normal and $T_3$ is self-adjoint.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Denote $\Delta_1=\Sigma_1\cap \sigma(T)$ and $\Delta_2=\Sigma_2\cap \sigma(T)$. Then $\sigma(T)=\Delta_1\cup (-\Delta_1^*)\cup \Delta_2$. Denote $\mathcal{H}_1=\text{ran} E_T(\Delta_1)$, $\mathcal{H}_2=\text{ran}E_T(-\Delta_1^*)$, and $\mathcal{H}_3=\text{ran}E_{T}(\Delta_2)$. Then $\mathcal{H}=\mathcal{H}_1\oplus\mathcal{H}_2\oplus\mathcal{H}_3$. Since $T$ is normal, the subspaces $\mathcal{H}_1,\mathcal{H}_2,\mathcal{H}_3$ reduces $T$. Then $T=T_1\oplus T_2\oplus T_3$, where $T_i =P_{\mathcal{H}_i}T|_{\mathcal{H}_i}$. By \cref{key-lemma}, we have $C\mathcal{H}_1=\mathcal{H}_2$ and $C\mathcal{H}_2=\mathcal{H}_1$. Therefore, we have 
\[C=\begin{bmatrix}
0&D^{-1}&0\\
D&0&0\\
0&0&C_3
\end{bmatrix},\]
where $D:\mathcal{H}_1\rightarrow\mathcal{H}_2$ is an anti-linear, invertible, isometry, and $C_3:\mathcal{H}_3\rightarrow\mathcal{H}_3$ is a conjugation. Since $T$ satisfies $CTC=-T$, we have $T_2=-DT_1D^{-1}$. Again, $T_1$ is normal, so there exists a conjugation $C_1$ on $\mathcal{H}_1$ such that $C_1T_1C_1=T_1^*$, and hence we have $T_2=-DC_1T_1^*C_1D^{-1}$. Observe that $DC_1$ is an unitary operator. Thus $T_2\cong -T_1^*$ (unitarily equivalent).
head: environment

title: Corollary
body_md: Let $T\in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$ be a $C$-normal operator. Then  $S_1=T^*T-TT^*\cong N\oplus (-N^*) \oplus (iS)$, where $N$ is normal operator and $S$ is self-adjoint operator.

title: Remark
body_md: If $T\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$ is normal and $C$-normal, then have seen that $CT^*T=T^*TC$. Since $T^*T$ is complex symmetric with respect to some conjugation, say $K$. Then by using \cref{anti-commut-normal}, $C=BK$ for some $B\in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$, where $B$ is $K$-symmetric unitary operator satisfying $BT^*T=T^*TB$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: If $T$ is $C$-normal, then we have observed that the anti-linear operator $CT$ commutes with the linear operator $T^*T$. Since $T^*T$ is complex symmetric with some conjugation, say $K$, by using \cref{anti-commut-normal}, we can say that $CT=DK$ for some $D\in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$ such that $D$ commute with $T^*T$. This implies that $T=CDK$ for some conjugation $K$. To be more precise, if $T\in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$ is $C$-normal, then it can be written as $T=CDK$ for some $D\in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$ and conjugation $K$.

title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{singular value ineq}
Let $C$ be a conjugation, and $T$ be a compact $C$-normal operator, where $T=A+iB$ be the Cartesian decomposition of $T$. Then 
\[ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}s_j(|A|+|B|)\leq s_j(T)\leq s_j(|A|+|B|),  \]
for $j=1,2,\dots$.
